objective: Digital forensics basics: chain of custody, order of volatility, legal holds

The objectives PDF was not re-read; the objective wording (digital forensics: legal hold, chain of custody, acquisition, preservation, order of volatility) is the course seed's.

sources.cite: IETF RFC 3227 (BCP 55), Guidelines for Evidence Collection and Archiving
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'When collecting evidence you should proceed from the volatile to the less volatile': registers and cache; routing table, arp cache, process table, kernel statistics, memory; temporary file systems; disk; remote logging and monitoring data; physical configuration and network topology; archival media. Things to avoid: 'Don't shutdown until you've completed evidence collection'; 'Don't trust the programs on the system'; 'Don't run programs that modify the access time of all files on the system'. Chain of custody: 'You should be able to clearly describe how the evidence was found, how it was handled and everything that happened to it.' Privacy: 'Do not intrude on people's privacy without strong justification.'

Fictional company and people. The offboarding job, the times and the file sizes are the author's. Whether a hash, a write blocker or a legal hold is required in a given jurisdiction is a legal question; the scenario follows the general practice the objective names.

brief.situation: You are the security analyst at Corrin Turbines, a fictional manufacturer. At 10:00 legal calls: an engineer resigned yesterday to join a competitor, and DLP flagged design files copied to a USB drive last night. His laptop is on and locked at his desk with the drive still plugged in. IT's offboarding job runs at 11:00 for yesterday's leavers.
handover: You have a response kit: trusted collection tools on USB, write blockers and evidence bags.
Legal can place holds; HR handles any conversation with the engineer.
howItWorks: The console shows alerts, evidence events as they arrive, and the items at stake.
Each task takes your time: start it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The offboarding job keeps to its schedule on the same clock.
When you close the collection, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The nightly offboarding job for yesterday's leavers runs at 11:00, an hour after the 10:00 start.

writeup.question: For the record: what you preserved first, in what order you collected, and how the evidence stays trustworthy.

parts.label: Preserve
parts.criteria: Places the legal hold and pauses the job before 11:00, and opens the custody form before collecting.
parts.modelAnswer: Legal hold on the mailbox and cloud drive with the 11:00 offboarding job paused; custody form CC-0412 opened before I touched the laptop.

parts.label: Order
parts.criteria: Collects memory and live state with trusted tools before powering down and imaging the disk, then the USB drive.
parts.modelAnswer: Memory and live state first, from my kit, which showed a sync client uploading to a personal cloud account; then power down and image the disk through a write blocker; then the USB drive.

parts.label: Integrity
parts.criteria: Hashes every image, runs nothing on the suspect system, records each transfer, and does not tip off the employee.
parts.modelAnswer: SHA-256 of each original and image match and are on the form; I ran no programs on the laptop and changed no access times; legal and HR decide when to speak to him.

expertPath.text: DLP events; legal hold on mailbox and cloud drive, offboarding paused.
Custody form; memory and live state with the kit's tools (a personal cloud sync client is running).

preserved.headline: Good: evidence that will stand up
preserved.body: You stopped the scheduled deletion first, opened custody before touching anything, took memory before the disk with your own tools, and hashed every image. Legal and HR now decide how to speak to the engineer.

gaps.headline: Collected, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what weakens the case: memory lost to a shutdown, a late custody form, a missing image or a premature conversation.

destroyed.headline: Deleted on schedule
destroyed.body: The offboarding job did exactly what it was built to do. A legal hold and a paused job in the first minutes would have kept the mailbox and cloud drive.

tainted.headline: Tainted
tainted.body: Browsing and copying on the suspect system changed access times and ran untrusted programs. Collect with your own tools and examine the image, never the original.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Preserve first: a legal hold on the mailbox and cloud drive, with the 11:00 offboarding job paused for the account. Open the chain-of-custody form before touching anything. Collect from most to least volatile with trusted tools from your kit: memory and live state from the running laptop (which shows a sync client uploading to a personal cloud account), then power down and image the disk through a write blocker, then the USB drive; hash each original and image. Run nothing on the suspect system, do not shut it down before memory is taken, and do not confront the employee; brief legal and HR with the evidence list and hashes.
